regionalNotesEnglish: Qualified site-safety review is required for slippery roofs, lightning, stop-work triggers and descent/evacuation procedures.
Boot grip and any time or weather threshold in the English scene are not a universal safety clearance.
archivedDraft.status: separate unapproved draft; no answer, audio or progress inheritance

sourceDecisionQuestions.question: Footing/apoyo firme is physical stability on a roof, not a generic support or safe-condition certification. Archived appui and appui stable need qualified contextual French and roofing safety review before scored use.

Spanish relámpagos and English lightning may mean visible lightning activity; archived foudre can imply a strike or the phenomenon. Set a consistent French weather term without changing the source stop-work claim, and obtain qualified lightning safety review.
Source tormenta/storm is contextual; archived orage narrows to a thunderstorm. Confirm the intended weather event and descent message with source and qualified safety reviewers.

Dew/wet-roof footing, grip boots and stop-if-weather-changes commands are source examples, not general clearance to work on a wet roof or a universal stop threshold. Obtain qualified site/weather procedure review before selecting learner commands; keep any site plan in internal notes.

Archived speaking adds a site evacuation plan and confirmation from every member, beyond source speaking's warning about slick footing and descent when lightning approaches. Preserve source scope; separate proposed site procedure from learner-facing answer.
